summary: - _(f) Issue appropriate direction(s) / order (s) to the Respondents to return / release forthwith the Performance Bank Guarantees No: 0393BGFD002420 for Rs 15 crores respectively issued in its favour by the Petitioner;_ - _(a) Issue ex-parte ad interim orders/ directions to the Respondents not to act in any prejudicial manner to the rights and interest of the Petitioner, including, but not limited to:_ - _i. Encashment of the CBG issued by the Petitioner in favour of the Respondent No. 2 (in its erstwhile capacity of CTU);_ - _ii. Abstain itself from taking coercive and/ or precipitative actions pursuant to letters dated 03.09.2021 and 24.12.2021 herein till final disposal of the petition; and/or_ - _(d) Pass any such further/ other Orders as this Hon’ble Commission may deem fit in the interest of equity and justice._ **3.** The Commission during the hearing dated 05.09.2024, after considering the submissions of the Petitioner, directed the CTUIL shall not proceed to any take any coercive/precipitative action against the Petitioner in connection to the said invoices, - (hh) Although the Original LTA was operationalised by the CTUIL on 14.04.2019, due to the aforesaid underlying difficulties, the Petitioner was left in a precarious situation, wherein the Original LTA could not be utilised by it even though it was validly obtained. Hence, the aforesaid events clearly fall within the scope and ambit of force majeure, frustrating its ability to execute the project in a timely manner. Accordingly, as per the principle laid down by the APTEL in Appeal 266 of 2016, the Petitioner cannot be held liable for payment of any relinquishment charges. - (p) Insofar as the Petitioner’s plea regarding frustration of its PPA and the resultant inability to utilise the LTA is concerned, it is submitted that the said plea is also not admissible. The position has been well settled by this Commission in the judgments in Petition No. 195/MP/2019, 525/MP/2020 and 103/MP/2021, that there is no correlation between the commissioning of a generating station and the performance of obligations under the LTA Agreement. **9.** During the course of the hearing, the learned counsel for the Petitioner and Respondent. Considering the submissions of Petitioner and Respondent, the Commission reserved the matter for order. Subsequently, the matter was raised by the learned counsel for the CTUIL on 8.12.2023, and it was submitted that, since the validity of the BG issued by the Petitioner is expiring on 31.12.2023, the Petitioner should be directed to extend the validity of the BG. Accordingly, the Commission directed the Petitioner to keep the BG alive till the disposal of the instant Petition. **10.** The CTUIL and the Petitioner have filed their respective written submissions dated 04.01.2024 and 23.01.2024, wherein they have reiterated earlier submissions in the matter. **12.** Considering the submissions made by the parties, the Commission observed that keeping in view that the invoices raised by CTUIL towards the relinquishment charges dated 12.3.2024 are approaching their due date and the Petitioner apprehends the coercive/precipitative actions by CTUIL thereafter, the Commission, for balancing the interest of both the sides, deemed it appropriate to direct that CTUIL shall not proceed to take any such coercive/precipitative action against the Petitioner in connection to the said invoices, provided the Petitioner deposit 25% of the amount within two weeks from the date of issuance of the ROP. The Commission also directed CTUIL to file the following information and reserved the matter for order: - (d) In these circumstances, the then unified POWERGRID approached this Commission by filing a Petition [being Petition No.266/MP/2020] seeking permission of the Commission to defer raising of invoices for relinquishment charges. Even before the above Petition could be taken up for hearing on admission by the Commission, the Appellant in Appeal No.416/2020: Himachal Sorang Power Pvt. Ltd. Vs. Power Grid Corporation of India Ltd. & Anr. filed against the Order dated 8.3.2019 passed in Petition No.92/MP/2015, approached the Hon’ble Appellate Tribunal by filing IA No.943/2020 seeking stay of proceedings of the above Petition before this Hon’ble Commission. The contention was that the unified POWERGRID could not implement the Order dated 8.3.2019, as Appeals were pending before the Hon’ble Tribunal against the said Order, wherein substantial questions of law had been raised. Vide In this manner, the Hon’ble Tribunal restrained this Commission from considering prayer ‘b’ in the above-said Petition filed by the unified POWERGRID. Consequently, when Petition No.266/MP/2020 was listed for hearing on admission before this Commission on 7.8.2020, the unified POWERGRID sought permission from this Commission to withdraw the said Petition. This Commission disposed of the said Petition accordingly. **21.** Considering the submission of Petitioner and Respondent, the following issues arise for our consideration: **Issue No 3: Whether margins in the existing system would have an effect on the relinquishment charge for the Petitioner?** _154. The relevant observations of the Commission in order dated 12.7.2016 in the Petition No. 315/MP/2015 are extracted as under:_ ## **Issue No.3: Whether margins in the existing system would have an effect on the relinquishment charge for the Petitioner?**
